trace_name: Ulnar nerve decompression: unconfirmed release - persistent symptoms

errors.detail: release completed without confirming its completeness along the full length (m5.4 not performed); incomplete decompression is a named technical cause of failure after this operation (T34), and the sites an unconfirmed release leaves behind are the revision series' findings — arcade of Struthers 71.4%, deep flexor-pronator aponeurosis 38% (T35)

complications.detail: persistent symptoms declared as a postoperative consequence of the unconfirmed (incomplete) release (structural outcome; no physiology representation of entrapment exists in the engine, so no volume effect is computed)

description: [t=60s] m0.1: Review the referral, the electrodiagnostic confirmation, the symptom pattern and the McGowan grade; confirm ulnar neuropathy at the elbow and the indication for decompression

[t=120s] m0.2: Confirm consent and the operative plan: in-situ decompression as the primary configuration, with anterior transposition consented and planned should the stability assessment find the nerve unstable; consent covers injury to the medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve, including its painful-neuroma consequence
[t=180s] m0.3: Confirm team, resource tier and equipment plan for the case, including the operating microscope's availability should a nerve injury require repair
[t=240s] m0.4: Establish anaesthesia: brachial plexus block, the consulted cohort's standard anaesthetic for this operation
[t=300s] m0.5: Apply the pneumatic arm tourniquet for a bloodless, visualised field

[t=360s] m0.6: Position the patient supine with the arm on a hand table, the elbow free to range through full flexion and extension (the stability assessment requires the full range, intraoperatively)
[t=420s] m0.7: WHO Sign In completed before induction of anaesthesia

[t=480s] m0.8: Confirm that antibiotic prophylaxis is withheld: preoperative antibiotics do not demonstrate benefit for uncomplicated ulnar nerve release at the elbow (919 operations; infection 1.7% without vs 2.7% with prophylaxis, T33), so this procedure carries no prophylaxis microstep - the withholding is itself the authored, sourced act, and the process component's ceiling is 4 of 5 by design
[t=540s] m0.9: WHO Time Out completed immediately before skin incision
[t=600s] m1.1: Make the longitudinal skin incision along the course of the ulnar nerve, between the medial epicondyle and the olecranon

[t=660s] m1.2: Dissect through the subcutaneous layer under direct vision: the branches of the medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve cross this field, and the 8-10 cm incision this operation needs puts them at risk along its whole length (T29)

[t=720s] m1.3: Demonstrate the medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve and its branches identified in the subcutaneous plane and protected - held clear of the dissection and of every division line along the whole incision
[t=780s] m2.1: Demonstrate the ulnar nerve identified proximal to the cubital tunnel, in undisected tissue, and protected under a vessel loop before any fascial structure is divided
[t=840s] m2.2: Review the operative findings at the elbow and confirm the plan to proceed: in-situ decompression primary, transposition reserved for instability at the stability assessment
[t=900s] dp1 -> proceed-in-situ

[t=960s] m2.3: Demonstrate the full release extent established before any division: proximally to the arcade of Struthers, through the cubital tunnel, and distally through the flexor carpi ulnaris aponeurosis until the motor branches - the nerve under direct vision along the whole length to be released
[t=960s] Nerves at risk identified and protected before division of the cubital tunnel fascia achieved: all three criteria demonstrated
[t=1020s] m3.1: Confirm the cubital tunnel retinaculum (Osborne's ligament) is fully exposed, with the protected nerve seen entering the tunnel
[t=1080s] m3.2: Second look: re-confirm the identified nerve, the cutaneous-branch account and the release extent before division
[t=1140s] m3.3: Pre-division pause: the identified nerve, the branch account and the release extent are confirmed aloud before any fascial structure is divided

[t=1200s] m4.1: Divide the arcade of Struthers and the proximal fascia, when present, as part of the proximal decompression - an unreleased arcade is the commonest proximal finding at revision (71.4%, T35)
[t=1260s] m5.1: Divide Osborne's ligament (the cubital tunnel retinaculum) over the protected nerve
[t=1320s] m5.2: Release the aponeurotic band between the humeral and ulnar heads of flexor carpi ulnaris, continuing the distal decompression until the motor branches are visualised
[t=1380s] m5.3: Release the deep flexor-pronator aponeurosis, the distal limit of a complete decompression (residual compression at this site in 38% of revisions, T35)

[t=1440s] m6.1: Range the elbow through full flexion and extension and dynamically assess the released nerve's stability in the sulcus - the consulted protocol's decision point: instability or subluxation routes to transposition, preserved stability completes the decompression alone (T31)
[t=1500s] dp5 -> complete-in-situ
[t=1560s] m6.2: In-situ completion: confirm the nerve lies stable in the sulcus through the full range, untethered and under no tension
[t=1620s] m7.1: Deflate the tourniquet, achieve haemostasis and inspect the wound
[t=1680s] m7.2: Re-inspect the ulnar nerve along the whole released length and the medial antebrachial cutaneous branches at the end of the case
[t=1740s] m8.1: Close the subcutaneous layer and the skin (the tunnel is left open - that is the release)
[t=1800s] m8.2: Confirm the postoperative plan: active elbow range-of-motion exercises from postoperative day 3; after submuscular transposition, avoid forceful gripping for approximately three weeks
[t=1860s] m8.3: WHO Sign Out completed before the patient leaves the operating room
[t=1920s] complication recognised: incomplete-release
[t=1980s] dp4 -> return-theatre
plus: The nerves at risk were identified and protected before any fascia was divided — ulnar nerve demonstrated and protected, medial antebrachial cutaneous branches accounted for, full release extent established (T29, T31, T34).
Pre-division pause performed and the identification confirmed with the team before division (module safety culture, T20).
All three WHO checklist phases were completed at their integration points (T6).
delta: err.incomplete-release — release completed without confirming its completeness along the full length (m5.4 not performed); incomplete decompression is a named technical cause of failure after this operation (T34), and the sites an unconfirmed release leaves behind are the revision series' findings — arcade of Struthers 71.4%, deep flexor-pronator aponeurosis 38% (T35)
directive: Confirm the release before closing: the elevator must pass freely and the nerve must glide from the arcade of Struthers to the flexor-pronator aponeurosis — incomplete decompression is a named technical cause of failure, and the revision series finds the missed sites in most failed cases (T34; T35).
summary: Verdict: PASS (formative only — no construct evidence exists for these scores yet).
Checklist 96.7% (29/30), safety gate 4/4, process 4/5, physiology 7/7, management 5/5.

Next focus: err.incomplete-release — release completed without confirming its completeness along the full length (m5.4 not performed); incomplete decompression is a named technical cause of failure after this operation (T34), and the sites an unconfirmed release leaves behind are the revision series' findings — arcade of Struthers 71.4%, deep flexor-pronator aponeurosis 38% (T35)
